messages.content:
FontRoxor edits — pass one to apply_edit as {"edit": {...}}.

Every edit has a "type" (camelCase) and its fields (camelCase). "glyph" is always a glyph INDEX
(get it from list_glyphs or get_glyph). Coordinates are font units, y axis UP, baseline at y = 0.

HOW A CONTOUR IS WRITTEN
  {"closed": true, "points": [[50, 0, "l"], [150, 0, "l"], [150, 700, "l"], [50, 700, "l"]]}
  A point is [x, y, kind], or [x, y, kind, true] when it is smooth (its two handles aligned).
  This is how get_glyph gives them and how you write them. Each on-curve point carries the
  kind of the segment that ARRIVES on it:
    "l"  line     a straight segment from the previous on-curve point
    "c"  curve    a cubic Bézier: its two control points come just BEFORE it, kind "o"
    "q"  qcurve   a quadratic spline: one or more "o" points come just before it
    "o"  offcurve a control point
    "m"  move     the first point of an OPEN contour only
  A closed contour is cyclic: the controls of the segment arriving on points[0] are the LAST
  points of the list. Only CLOSED contours are exported. The outside of a shape and its
  holes turn in opposite directions (correctDirection fixes that for you). Put a point at
  each extreme of a curve (top, bottom, left, right) — addExtremes does it for you.
  The example above is a 100-unit stem from the baseline to y = 700. A round dot:
    {"closed": true, "points": [[100, 50, "c", true], [128, 50, "o"], [150, 72, "o"], [150, 100, "c", true],
       [150, 128, "o"], [128, 150, "o"], [100, 150, "c", true], [72, 150, "o"], [50, 128, "o"], [50, 100, "c", true], [50, 72, "o"], [72, 50, "o"]]}
  (the last two "o" are the controls of the curve arriving on the first point).
  Wherever an edit takes "glyph", its index or its name are both accepted.

WHAT YOU ACT ON (there is no selection to make first: you name the target)
  a point      {contour, point}: its two indices in get_glyph             movePoints, setPoints, deletePoints, setSmooth, setContinuity
  a segment    the {contour, point} of the on-curve point it ARRIVES on   deleteSegments, insertPoint
  a contour    its index in get_glyph                                     reverseContours, boolean, the transform and copy_contours tools
  a face       any point [x, y] inside the region of ink                  eraseFace, moveFace
  the glyph    nothing more                                               setContours, transform, removeOverlap, correctDirection…

DRAWING
  setContours      {glyph, contours: [contour...]}        replaces ALL the outlines of a glyph at once — the best way to draw
  addShape         {glyph, shape: "rectangle"|"ellipse", frame: [x0, y0, x1, y1]}
  addStroke        {glyph, points: [[x, y]...], width}    a brush stroke — prefer the brush_stroke tool, which names the brushes
  setRules         {rules: [{name, conditions: [[{axis, min?, max?}]], substitutions: [[from, to]], last}]}
                   the rules of the axes, the whole list: in each region (bounds per axis tag, in axis values; a
                   missing bound is the axis's own), glyphs are replaced by others in the variable font (rvrn, or
                   rclt when last). get_design shows them.
  setKernModels    {models: [[first, second]...]}         the model pairs of the kerning, by glyph name, the whole list (propose_kern_models adds some)
  setKernAuto      {pairs: [[first key, second key]...]}   the kerning pairs the automatic kerning made (it may redo them); any other pair is the designer's
  setView          {part, value}   what a tab keeps with the project ("preview": its text, size, page, ground…); set it with show_in_window rather than by hand
  setStroke        {glyph, stroke, width?, spine?}         retouch a brush stroke that is still a stroke (get_glyph lists them under
                   "strokes", by rank): another width, or another centre line ("spine": an open contour). Its shape is redrawn in
                   place. A stroke whose shape was edited by hand is no longer a stroke.
  setPoints        {glyph, points: [{contour, point, x, y}...]}   moves points to absolute positions
  movePoints       {glyph, points: [{contour, point}...], dx, dy}
  insertPoint      {glyph, contour, point, t}             on the segment arriving at "point", at t in 0..1
  deletePoints     {glyph, points: [{contour, point}...]} the outline closes around them
  setSmooth        {glyph, points: [...], smooth}
  setContinuity    {glyph, points: [...], continuity: "corner"|"smooth"|"curvature"} — curvature keeps the same curvature on both sides from then on (G2): the point stays, its handles adjust after every edit; next to a line, the curve's far control comes onto the tangent
  simplify         {glyph, points?: [...], tolerance} — remove superfluous points keeping the shape within tolerance (font units; 2 for a 1000 em): corners, extremes and line-to-curve joints stay, curves are refitted, near-duplicate points (a scan) merge
  transform        {glyph, points: null | [...], matrix: [xx, xy, yx, yy, dx, dy]}   null = the whole glyph.
                   Prefer the transform TOOL: it takes degrees, factors and a pivot, and builds the matrix.
  reverseContours  {glyph, contours: [index...]}
  setStartPoint    {glyph, contour, point}                a point on the curve becomes the start of its closed contour
  setSegmentKind   {glyph, contour, point, curve}         the segment arriving at "point" becomes straight (false) or a curve (true)
  setBrush         {glyph, brush}                         makes a work glyph a brush shape of the project ({label, order}: its name and place in the list), or null to make it ordinary again; its box is 0 to the em long and half an em each side of the baseline
  setTension       {glyph, segments, tension}             cubic curves (each by the point it arrives at) get their handles at "tension" (0 to 1.5, about 0.55 is round) of the way to where the two tangents cross; directions kept
  correctDirection {glyph}        removeOverlap {glyph}        addExtremes {glyph}        tidy {glyph}
  boolean          {glyph, op: "union"|"subtract"|"intersect"|"exclude", contours: [index...]}
                   the listed contours are the tool, the other closed contours the matter
  roundCorners     {glyph, points: [], radius}            [] = every corner
  sharpenCorners   {glyph, points: []}
  harmonize        {glyph, points: [], keepNode: false}   [] = every smooth point between two curves: each
                   slides along its tangent until the curvature is the same on both sides (G2);
                   keepNode: true keeps the point where it is and slides its two handles instead

  appendPoint      {glyph, contour: null | index, x, y, handleIn: null | [x, y], handleOut: null | [x, y], smooth}
                   the pen: adds a point at the end of an OPEN contour (null starts a new one)
  closeContour     {glyph, contour}
  slice            {glyph, from: [x, y], to: [x, y]}      the knife: cuts every closed contour the line crosses right through
  deleteSegments   {glyph, segments: [{contour, point}...]}   removes the segment arriving at each point; the contour opens there
  eraseFace        {glyph, x, y}                           removes the region of ink that contains this point
  moveFace         {glyph, x, y, dx, dy}                   detaches that region and moves it

GUIDES AND TRACING IMAGE
  setGuides        {glyph, guides: [{x, y, angle}...]}    the whole list of the glyph's guides; angle 0 is horizontal, 90 vertical
  setBackground    {glyph, background: null}              removes the image the user traces over (adding one is the user's job)
  placeBackground  {glyph, x, y, width, height, opacity, locked}   moves or fades that image

METRICS
  setAdvance       {glyph, advance}
  setSidebearings  {glyph, left: number|null, right: number|null}   accented letters built on it follow
  setKerning       {first, second, value: number|null}    names of glyphs, or "@group"; null removes the pair
  setKernGroups    {glyph, left: string|null, right: string|null}

GLYPHS
  addGlyph         {unicodes: ["U+00E9"], compose: true}   name and advance are deduced when you leave them out.
                   Give characters as "U+00E9" or "é" (a number works too, in DECIMAL — do not convert by hand).
                   compose: true builds it from other glyphs when the font can ("é" = "e" + acute)
  compose          {glyph}        builds an EMPTY glyph the same way
  setGlyphMeta     {glyph, name, unicodes: ["U+00E9"]}
  deleteGlyph      {glyph}        refused while another glyph uses it as a component
  setExported      {glyph, exported}   false = a working piece, kept out of the exported font

COMPONENTS AND ANCHORS
  addComponent     {glyph, base: "name of the base glyph", matrix: [1, 0, 0, 1, dx, dy]}
  setComponent     {glyph, component, matrix}      removeComponents {glyph, components: [index...]}
  decompose        {glyph, components: null | [index...]}     turns components into contours
  setSmart         {glyph, smart: null | {axes: [{name, min, max, default}...], poles: [{glyph, location: {axisName: value}}...]}}
                   a SMART COMPONENT: the glyph has its own axes (the width of a stem, the depth of a
                   notch) and other drawings of itself at places on them; each pole is another glyph
  addSmartDrawing  {glyph, location: {axisName: value}}   creates that other drawing (a copy of the glyph,
                   not exported) at that place: then reshape it with setContours / movePoints etc.
                   It must keep the same points in the same order, or it is ignored
  addColorLayer    {glyph, color: paletteIndex}   a COLOR GLYPH: adds a layer on top — a new glyph (a copy of
                   this one, named {name}.colorN) drawn in that color; reshape it like any glyph.
                   The glyph's own drawing stays the one shown where color is not supported
  setColorLayers   {glyph, layers: [{glyph: "layer glyph name", color: paletteIndex | 65535 = text color,
                   alpha: 0..1, fill: null | gradient, blend: "normal"}...]}   the whole list, bottom to top.
                   gradient (font units, y up): {kind: "linear", start: [x, y], end: [x, y], stops, extend}
                   | {kind: "radial", start, startRadius, end, endRadius, stops, extend}
                   | {kind: "sweep", center, startAngle, endAngle (degrees, counterclockwise), stops, extend}
                   stops: [{offset: 0..1, color: paletteIndex, alpha: 0..1}...], extend: "pad" | "repeat" | "reflect"
                   blend: normal multiply screen overlay darken lighten colorDodge colorBurn hardLight softLight
                   difference exclusion hue saturation color luminosity plus atop inside outside erase keep xor
                   clip?: {glyph: "another glyph", keep: true | false}: the layer is painted only inside that
                   glyph (keep) or only outside it — how a hand-painted decor keeps varying in a variable font
  flattenColorLayer {glyph, layer}   the clipped layer becomes its exact clipped shape in every master
                   (it no longer varies); flatten_color_layer also removes the clipping glyph if unused
                   (a gradient, an alpha or a blend writes COLR version 1). The colors are setFontInfo's
                   palettes: [[[r, g, b, a]...]...] (0-255), the first palette is the default one
                   decor (setFontInfo's info.decor): a recipe drawn on EVERY letter, exported as color
                   layers, outlines untouched — {effects: [...]} listed from top to bottom, each
                   {kind, visible, paint: {color: paletteIndex, alpha, gradient?: {kind: "linear" |
                   "radial", angle (degrees, 90 = bottom to top), stops, extend}, alternates?: [paletteIndex]
                   (each letter takes its own color among color and these)}, blend?} with kind
                   "fill" | "outline" {width, side: "outside"|"inside"|"center"} | "shadow" {dx, dy}
                   | "extrude" {depth, angle} | "inline" {inset, width} | "innerShadow" {dx, dy} (the
                   letter minus its shifted copy) | "rings" {width, gap, count} | "stripes" {angle,
                   period, width} | "dots" {period, size, angle, grow (-1..1: dots grow toward the
                   bottom)} | "slices" {height, shift} | "rough" {amount, size} (worn edge, like a
                   stamp) | "stencil" {width, period, angle} (bridges cut through) | "pattern"
                   {glyph (a glyph of the font drawn as the motif, see pattern_from_svg), mode:
                   "inside"|"cut"|"free", repeat (bool), size (scale), angle, x, y (single: place
                   in the letter's ink box, 0..1; repeated: grid offset), gap}. Each effect may
                   carry vary (0..1): its numbers, its opacity (only lower) and its gradient's angle and
                   centre change a little from one letter to the next,
                   always the same way for a given letter. A gradient sits the same on
                   every letter (its box: the advance, from the baseline to the cap height).
                   decor_preset sets a ready-made one. decor.letters: {glyphName: [effects]} gives a
                   letter its own stack instead of the font's. A glyph with its own color layers keeps them
  setMasterDecor   {master, effects: [kind objects] | null}   the decor geometry of one master of a
                   variable font (a longer shadow in the bold): the recipe's effects, same order,
                   only their numbers ({kind: "shadow", dx, dy}, {kind: "outline", width, side}…);
                   null gives the master back the recipe's. Colors stay the recipe's
  detachDecor      {glyph}   paint a letter by hand: the decor the recipe gives it becomes its own
                   color layers, drawn in every master (the decor_detach action does the same)
  paintFace        {glyph, x, y, color}   the paint bucket: the region of ink around (x, y) becomes a
                   color layer of palette color `color` on top (the glyph keeps its drawing below, in
                   the text color); a face already painted changes color
  setSmartValues   {glyph, component, values: {axisName: value}}   places a component on the axes of
                   its smart base: it receives the drawing taken between the poles
  setAnchors       {glyph, anchors: [{name: "top", x, y}...]}   the whole list; "top" on a letter
                   receives "_top" of an accent. Built accented letters follow the anchor.
  setHints         {glyph, hints: [...]}   the whole list of manual hinting for small sizes on
                   screens, each point given as {contour, point}. Hints are added to the
                   hinting the glyph already has (the original file's, or the automatic one):
                   {type:"align", at}           the point snaps to the nearest zone (baseline,
                                                x-height…), or to the nearest pixel row;
                   {type:"stem", from, to}      the stroke between two points keeps a whole
                                                number of pixels, one at least;
                   {type:"delta", at, ppem, shift}  moves the point by shift eighths of a pixel
                                                (-8..8, up if positive) at that size only (6..53).
                   Add axis:"x" to any of them for the horizontal direction (columns; a delta
                   then moves right if positive). Horizontal hints only show in black-and-white
                   rendering: ClearType and DirectWrite ignore them.
                   An empty list gives the glyph back to the hinting it had.

WHOLE FONT
  setFontInfo      {info: {...}}  the WHOLE record, exactly as get_font_info returns it, with your changes
  setFeatures      {text}  the whole OpenType feature text (Adobe feature language); prefer set_features, which reports errors
  derive           {derivation: {weight, contrast, slant, width, tracking, method: "optical"|"geometric"}}
                   shows a derived style of the whole font without touching its outlines:
                   weight 0.5 = stems 50 % thicker (from -0.9 to 3; a bold is about 0.5 to 0.9),
                   contrast from -1 to 1 (above 0: thicker thicks, thinner thins), slant in degrees
                   (-45 to 45; an oblique is about 12), width -0.1 = 10 % narrower (-0.7 to 1),
                   tracking in fractions of the em (-0.3 to 1). method "optical" (default) does
                   what type designers do, "geometric" moves the outline evenly. All zero = back
                   to the original.
  align            {glyph, points, how}   aligns or spreads what the points designate: when they
                   are ALL the points of two contours or more, the contours move as whole shapes
                   (by their boxes, equal gaps between them); otherwise the on-curve points move,
                   with their handles. how = left, center, right, top, middle, bottom,
                   distributeX, distributeY (three at least).
  alignMasters     {glyphs}       in the other masters, puts these glyphs back in the order of the
                   master being edited (contour order, start point, direction): no point moves.
                   For glyphs check_font reports as masterOrder.
  redrawMasters    {glyphs}       redraws these glyphs in the other masters from the master being
                   edited, derived for each master's place. It REPLACES their drawing there: use it
                   for glyphs check_font reports as masterShape, and say that you did.
  consolidate      {}             turns the derived style into the real outlines. While a style
                   is derived, outline edits are refused: consolidate first.

MASTERS (a variable font: several masters of the same glyphs, and every style in between)
  setDesign        {axes: [{tag: "wght", name: "Weight", min: 100, default: 400, max: 900}...],
                    masters: [{name: "Regular", location: [400]}...]}
                   the whole list of axes, and the name and place of EVERY master, in order
                   (one value per axis). On a font with a single style: give one axis and one
                   master, it becomes the first. One master must sit at the default of every axis.
  addMaster        {name: "Bold", location: [700], derivation: null | {weight, ...}}
                   a copy of the master being edited, to redraw — or, with a derivation, that
                   master made bolder, narrower, slanted: same points, so it interpolates at once
  removeMaster     {index}        not the one being edited
  switchMaster     {index}        the master every other edit and tool then works on. Glyphs must
                   keep the same contours and points in every master to vary: read get_design.

SEVERAL AT ONCE
  batch            {edits: [edit...]}   applied entirely or not at all, undone in one step

messages.content:
FontRoxor edits — pass one to apply_edit as {"edit": {...}}.

Every edit has a "type" (camelCase) and its fields (camelCase). "glyph" is always a glyph INDEX
(get it from list_glyphs or get_glyph). Coordinates are font units, y axis UP, baseline at y = 0.

HOW A CONTOUR IS WRITTEN
  {"closed": true, "points": [[50, 0, "l"], [150, 0, "l"], [150, 700, "l"], [50, 700, "l"]]}
  A point is [x, y, kind], or [x, y, kind, true] when it is smooth (its two handles aligned).
  This is how get_glyph gives them and how you write them. Each on-curve point carries the
  kind of the segment that ARRIVES on it:
    "l"  line     a straight segment from the previous on-curve point
    "c"  curve    a cubic Bézier: its two control points come just BEFORE it, kind "o"
    "q"  qcurve   a quadratic spline: one or more "o" points come just before it
    "o"  offcurve a control point
    "m"  move     the first point of an OPEN contour only
  A closed contour is cyclic: the controls of the segment arriving on points[0] are the LAST
  points of the list. Only CLOSED contours are exported. The outside of a shape and its
  holes turn in opposite directions (correctDirection fixes that for you). Put a point at
  each extreme of a curve (top, bottom, left, right) — addExtremes does it for you.
  The example above is a 100-unit stem from the baseline to y = 700. A round dot:
    {"closed": true, "points": [[100, 50, "c", true], [128, 50, "o"], [150, 72, "o"], [150, 100, "c", true],
       [150, 128, "o"], [128, 150, "o"], [100, 150, "c", true], [72, 150, "o"], [50, 128, "o"], [50, 100, "c", true], [50, 72, "o"], [72, 50, "o"]]}
  (the last two "o" are the controls of the curve arriving on the first point).
  Wherever an edit takes "glyph", its index or its name are both accepted.

WHAT YOU ACT ON (there is no selection to make first: you name the target)
  a point      {contour, point}: its two indices in get_glyph             movePoints, setPoints, deletePoints, setSmooth, setContinuity
  a segment    the {contour, point} of the on-curve point it ARRIVES on   deleteSegments, insertPoint
  a contour    its index in get_glyph                                     reverseContours, boolean, the transform and copy_contours tools
  a face       any point [x, y] inside the region of ink                  eraseFace, moveFace
  the glyph    nothing more                                               setContours, transform, removeOverlap, correctDirection…

DRAWING
  setContours      {glyph, contours: [contour...]}        replaces ALL the outlines of a glyph at once — the best way to draw
  addShape         {glyph, shape: "rectangle"|"ellipse", frame: [x0, y0, x1, y1]}
  addStroke        {glyph, points: [[x, y]...], width}    a brush stroke — prefer the brush_stroke tool, which names the brushes
  setRules         {rules: [{name, conditions: [[{axis, min?, max?}]], substitutions: [[from, to]], last}]}
                   the rules of the axes, the whole list: in each region (bounds per axis tag, in axis values; a
                   missing bound is the axis's own), glyphs are replaced by others in the variable font (rvrn, or
                   rclt when last). get_design shows them.
  setKernModels    {models: [[first, second]...]}         the model pairs of the kerning, by glyph name, the whole list (propose_kern_models adds some)
  setKernAuto      {pairs: [[first key, second key]...]}   the kerning pairs the automatic kerning made (it may redo them); any other pair is the designer's
  setView          {part, value}   what a tab keeps with the project ("preview": its text, size, page, ground…); set it with show_in_window rather than by hand
  setStroke        {glyph, stroke, width?, spine?}         retouch a brush stroke that is still a stroke (get_glyph lists them under
                   "strokes", by rank): another width, or another centre line ("spine": an open contour). Its shape is redrawn in
                   place. A stroke whose shape was edited by hand is no longer a stroke.
  setPoints        {glyph, points: [{contour, point, x, y}...]}   moves points to absolute positions
  movePoints       {glyph, points: [{contour, point}...], dx, dy}
  insertPoint      {glyph, contour, point, t}             on the segment arriving at "point", at t in 0..1
  deletePoints     {glyph, points: [{contour, point}...]} the outline closes around them
  setSmooth        {glyph, points: [...], smooth}
  setContinuity    {glyph, points: [...], continuity: "corner"|"smooth"|"curvature"} — curvature keeps the same curvature on both sides from then on (G2): the point stays, its handles adjust after every edit; next to a line, the curve's far control comes onto the tangent
  simplify         {glyph, points?: [...], tolerance} — remove superfluous points keeping the shape within tolerance (font units; 2 for a 1000 em): corners, extremes and line-to-curve joints stay, curves are refitted, near-duplicate points (a scan) merge
  transform        {glyph, points: null | [...], matrix: [xx, xy, yx, yy, dx, dy]}   null = the whole glyph.
                   Prefer the transform TOOL: it takes degrees, factors and a pivot, and builds the matrix.
  reverseContours  {glyph, contours: [index...]}
  setStartPoint    {glyph, contour, point}                a point on the curve becomes the start of its closed contour
  setSegmentKind   {glyph, contour, point, curve}         the segment arriving at "point" becomes straight (false) or a curve (true)
  setBrush         {glyph, brush}                         makes a work glyph a brush shape of the project ({label, order}: its name and place in the list), or null to make it ordinary again; its box is 0 to the em long and half an em each side of the baseline
  setTension       {glyph, segments, tension}             cubic curves (each by the point it arrives at) get their handles at "tension" (0 to 1.5, about 0.55 is round) of the way to where the two tangents cross; directions kept
  correctDirection {glyph}        removeOverlap {glyph}        addExtremes {glyph}        tidy {glyph}
  boolean          {glyph, op: "union"|"subtract"|"intersect"|"exclude", contours: [index...]}
                   the listed contours are the tool, the other closed contours the matter
  roundCorners     {glyph, points: [], radius}            [] = every corner
  sharpenCorners   {glyph, points: []}
  harmonize        {glyph, points: [], keepNode: false}   [] = every smooth point between two curves: each
                   slides along its tangent until the curvature is the same on both sides (G2);
                   keepNode: true keeps the point where it is and slides its two handles instead

  appendPoint      {glyph, contour: null | index, x, y, handleIn: null | [x, y], handleOut: null | [x, y], smooth}
                   the pen: adds a point at the end of an OPEN contour (null starts a new one)
  closeContour     {glyph, contour}
  slice            {glyph, from: [x, y], to: [x, y]}      the knife: cuts every closed contour the line crosses right through
  deleteSegments   {glyph, segments: [{contour, point}...]}   removes the segment arriving at each point; the contour opens there
  eraseFace        {glyph, x, y}                           removes the region of ink that contains this point
  moveFace         {glyph, x, y, dx, dy}                   detaches that region and moves it

GUIDES AND TRACING IMAGE
  setGuides        {glyph, guides: [{x, y, angle}...]}    the whole list of the glyph's guides; angle 0 is horizontal, 90 vertical
  setBackground    {glyph, background: null}              removes the image the user traces over (adding one is the user's job)
  placeBackground  {glyph, x, y, width, height, opacity, locked}   moves or fades that image

METRICS
  setAdvance       {glyph, advance}
  setSidebearings  {glyph, left: number|null, right: number|null}   accented letters built on it follow
  setKerning       {first, second, value: number|null}    names of glyphs, or "@group"; null removes the pair
  setKernGroups    {glyph, left: string|null, right: string|null}

GLYPHS
  addGlyph         {unicodes: ["U+00E9"], compose: true}   name and advance are deduced when you leave them out.
                   Give characters as "U+00E9" or "é" (a number works too, in DECIMAL — do not convert by hand).
                   compose: true builds it from other glyphs when the font can ("é" = "e" + acute)
  compose          {glyph}        builds an EMPTY glyph the same way
  setGlyphMeta     {glyph, name, unicodes: ["U+00E9"]}
  deleteGlyph      {glyph}        refused while another glyph uses it as a component
  setExported      {glyph, exported}   false = a working piece, kept out of the exported font

COMPONENTS AND ANCHORS
  addComponent     {glyph, base: "name of the base glyph", matrix: [1, 0, 0, 1, dx, dy]}
  setComponent     {glyph, component, matrix}      removeComponents {glyph, components: [index...]}
  decompose        {glyph, components: null | [index...]}     turns components into contours
  setSmart         {glyph, smart: null | {axes: [{name, min, max, default}...], poles: [{glyph, location: {axisName: value}}...]}}
                   a SMART COMPONENT: the glyph has its own axes (the width of a stem, the depth of a
                   notch) and other drawings of itself at places on them; each pole is another glyph
  addSmartDrawing  {glyph, location: {axisName: value}}   creates that other drawing (a copy of the glyph,
                   not exported) at that place: then reshape it with setContours / movePoints etc.
                   It must keep the same points in the same order, or it is ignored
  addColorLayer    {glyph, color: paletteIndex}   a COLOR GLYPH: adds a layer on top — a new glyph (a copy of
                   this one, named {name}.colorN) drawn in that color; reshape it like any glyph.
                   The glyph's own drawing stays the one shown where color is not supported
  setColorLayers   {glyph, layers: [{glyph: "layer glyph name", color: paletteIndex | 65535 = text color,
                   alpha: 0..1, fill: null | gradient, blend: "normal"}...]}   the whole list, bottom to top.
                   gradient (font units, y up): {kind: "linear", start: [x, y], end: [x, y], stops, extend}
                   | {kind: "radial", start, startRadius, end, endRadius, stops, extend}
                   | {kind: "sweep", center, startAngle, endAngle (degrees, counterclockwise), stops, extend}
                   stops: [{offset: 0..1, color: paletteIndex, alpha: 0..1}...], extend: "pad" | "repeat" | "reflect"
                   blend: normal multiply screen overlay darken lighten colorDodge colorBurn hardLight softLight
                   difference exclusion hue saturation color luminosity plus atop inside outside erase keep xor
                   clip?: {glyph: "another glyph", keep: true | false}: the layer is painted only inside that
                   glyph (keep) or only outside it — how a hand-painted decor keeps varying in a variable font
  flattenColorLayer {glyph, layer}   the clipped layer becomes its exact clipped shape in every master
                   (it no longer varies); flatten_color_layer also removes the clipping glyph if unused
                   (a gradient, an alpha or a blend writes COLR version 1). The colors are setFontInfo's
                   palettes: [[[r, g, b, a]...]...] (0-255), the first palette is the default one
                   decor (setFontInfo's info.decor): a recipe drawn on EVERY letter, exported as color
                   layers, outlines untouched — {effects: [...]} listed from top to bottom, each
                   {kind, visible, paint: {color: paletteIndex, alpha, gradient?: {kind: "linear" |
                   "radial", angle (degrees, 90 = bottom to top), stops, extend}, alternates?: [paletteIndex]
                   (each letter takes its own color among color and these)}, blend?} with kind
                   "fill" | "outline" {width, side: "outside"|"inside"|"center"} | "shadow" {dx, dy}
                   | "extrude" {depth, angle} | "inline" {inset, width} | "innerShadow" {dx, dy} (the
                   letter minus its shifted copy) | "rings" {width, gap, count} | "stripes" {angle,
                   period, width} | "dots" {period, size, angle, grow (-1..1: dots grow toward the
                   bottom)} | "slices" {height, shift} | "rough" {amount, size} (worn edge, like a
                   stamp) | "stencil" {width, period, angle} (bridges cut through) | "pattern"
                   {glyph (a glyph of the font drawn as the motif, see pattern_from_svg), mode:
                   "inside"|"cut"|"free", repeat (bool), size (scale), angle, x, y (single: place
                   in the letter's ink box, 0..1; repeated: grid offset), gap}. Each effect may
                   carry vary (0..1): its numbers, its opacity (only lower) and its gradient's angle and
                   centre change a little from one letter to the next,
                   always the same way for a given letter. A gradient sits the same on
                   every letter (its box: the advance, from the baseline to the cap height).
                   decor_preset sets a ready-made one. decor.letters: {glyphName: [effects]} gives a
                   letter its own stack instead of the font's. A glyph with its own color layers keeps them
  setMasterDecor   {master, effects: [kind objects] | null}   the decor geometry of one master of a
                   variable font (a longer shadow in the bold): the recipe's effects, same order,
                   only their numbers ({kind: "shadow", dx, dy}, {kind: "outline", width, side}…);
                   null gives the master back the recipe's. Colors stay the recipe's
  detachDecor      {glyph}   paint a letter by hand: the decor the recipe gives it becomes its own
                   color layers, drawn in every master (the decor_detach action does the same)
  paintFace        {glyph, x, y, color}   the paint bucket: the region of ink around (x, y) becomes a
                   color layer of palette color `color` on top (the glyph keeps its drawing below, in
                   the text color); a face already painted changes color
  setSmartValues   {glyph, component, values: {axisName: value}}   places a component on the axes of
                   its smart base: it receives the drawing taken between the poles

- **§, &, @, \*, #** — tracés à la plume, cohérents ;
- **æ** — ligature construite par composition (a + e entrelacés), pas étirée.

La vérification ne signale que des *conseils* (« overlap », « extremes »), normaux ici car les traits se croisent volontairement : je les laisse tels quels, les fusionner casserait les enchaînements.

Reste à trancher, en attente de l'original Mesrine : **Q** (boucle O + queue), et si tu veux, je peux aussi poser **œ / Œ** par composition comme pour æ.

Panneau style — police « manuscrit Mesrine »

Écriture : ronde et cursive, manuscrite ; tracés à la plume (nib) angle ~35°, épaississement variable (épais/très fin), pointes qui montent en boucle (arcs et becs).
Pas de blocs typographiques : chaque lettre a des queues, des boucles, des pointes obliques.

Métriques (mesurées) : baseline réel des pieds y=-5 (les pieds ne reposent pas sur 0) ; x-height 245 ; grandeurs de 856 ; ascendent 746 ; descendent -369 ; dépassement des rondes ~ -42.

Choix déjà faits par l'assistant (à vérifier par l'utilisateur) :
- K, W, X, Z, k (basse), z (basse), 2, 6, 8 ont été ajoutés à la plume, dans l'esprit de l'écriture, MAIS ils ne sont pas des lettres originales de Mesrine : à valider ou à redessiner à partir du manuscrit.
- æ : refait à partir du a et du e originaux, liés comme en cursive (la sortie du a devient l'attaque du e) ; pas une lettre du manuscrit.
- Les lettres existantes (o, a, e, s, x, u, c, …) sont la référence de style ; les nouvelles doivent les imiter (nib 35°, pointes, boucles).
- En cours / à trancher : Q (boucle O + queue), œ et Œ (ligatures) — en attente de l'original Mesrine. Pour œ, faire comme æ : o + e liés.
- À faire seulement si demandé : espace (space) vide ; accents déjà composés automatiquement pour le français.

Règle : chaque nouvelle lettre part du tracé existant (copier/transformer) et garde nib 35°, même x-height, même dépassement, pieds à y=-5.
